summary.text: A 66-year-old man with coronary artery disease and prior three-vessel stenting, insulin-dependent type 2 diabetes and essential hypertension presented with palpitations, presyncope and intermittent chest pain for 4 days. He was tachycardic, and the electrocardiogram showed monomorphic ventricular tachycardia; blood count and metabolic profile were unremarkable and high-sensitivity troponin peaked at 156.

Ventricular tachycardia was initially aborted with intravenous amiodarone and lidocaine plus as-needed intravenous metoprolol, but he had three sustained episodes in the first 24 h of admission, qualifying as VT storm. After intensive care unit admission with multiple recurrences, it was ultimately controlled with procainamide.

Echocardiography showed LVEF 55%, a 14 mm septal diameter unchanged from prior studies and a 25 mmHg LVOT gradient; the coronary angiogram showed patent stents and non-obstructive disease. Cardiac MRI showed a septal diameter up to 18 mm with mid-myocardial late gadolinium enhancement, leading to septal hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and a suspected VT focus in the hypertrophic septum. Electrophysiology mapping was bypassed, and radiofrequency ablation was recommended before ICD placement.

Transcoronary ethanol ablation of the first septal branch was chosen and performed on Day 5, reducing the post-PVC LVOT gradient from 45 to 17 mmHg and abating the VT, with a new right bundle branch abnormality. An ICD was implanted and he was discharged on oral metoprolol; at 4 months five VT runs were aborted by antitachycardia pacing and amiodarone was started, and at 1 year he had one VT episode in 6 months, took amiodarone 100 mg daily and had no plans for further ablation.
